question: Before entering a curve you should:
options: a:Accelerate quickly.,b:Activate your turn signal.,c:Reduce your speed.,d:Brake hard in the curve.
note: Slow down before you enter the curve to maintain control; braking hard in the curve can cause loss of control.

question: Broken yellow pavement markings are used to:
options: a:Separate lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions where passing is allowed.,b:Mark the right edge of the roadway.,c:Indicate no passing zones.,d:Separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction.
note: Broken yellow lines separate opposing traffic and indicate passing is permitted when the way ahead is clear.

question: In dense fog you should slow down and use which lights?
options: a:Parking lights only.,b:High beam headlights.,c:Low beam headlights.,d:Emergency flashers only.
note: Use low beams in fog; high beams can reflect back and reduce visibility further.

question: When following a large truck, you should:
options: a:Stay farther behind than you would a passenger vehicle.,b:Attempt to stay directly beside the truck.,c:Keep no more than one car length behind.,d:Follow more closely because the truck blocks your view.
note: Keep extra space behind large trucks so you can see and stop safely; tailgating reduces your safety margin and may place you in the truck's blind spot.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you face a green signal but pedestrians remain in the intersection, you must:
options: a:Proceed only if turning right.,b:Wave the pedestrians on and continue.,c:Proceed because you have the right-of-way.,d:Yield to the pedestrians.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in the intersection even when the light is green and must yield when turning on a steady green.

question: If an oncoming driver fails to dim their headlights, where should you look?
options: a:Look toward the center of the roadway.,b:Toward the right side of the road.,c:Look straight ahead.
note: If an oncoming driver fails to dim lights, look toward the right side of the road to avoid being blinded and stay on course.

question: What is the safest action if you find the roadway ahead flooded?
options: a:Drive only in the center of the roadway.,b:Slam on the brakes.,c:Do not drive through the flooded area; turn around and find another route.
note: Never attempt to drive through floodwater. Even seemingly shallow water can hide hazards and stall your vehicle.

question: How is having a driver license classified?
options: a:A right.,b:A requirement.,c:A privilege.
note: Driving is a privilege that can be suspended or revoked if abused. Holders must obey traffic laws to retain that privilege.

question: Your vehicle can begin to hydroplane at speeds as low as approximately:
options: a:25 miles per hour.,b:35 miles per hour.,c:55 miles per hour.,d:45 miles per hour.
note: Hydroplaning can start at speeds near 35 mph on standing water as tires lose their ability to channel water away.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you approach a flashing red traffic light, you must:
options: a:Only stop if other vehicles are present.,b:Assume it will turn green soon and proceed.,c:Treat the intersection as if controlled by a stop sign.,d:Turn around and find another route.
note: A flashing red light requires a full stop and yielding, the same as a stop sign.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a steady green traffic light at an intersection allow you to do?
options: a:You may continue through the intersection at a safe and reasonable speed, if it is clear to do so.,b:Increase your speed.,c:Adjust your mirrors.
note: A steady green light indicates you may proceed when the intersection is clear, but yield to traffic or pedestrians already in the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What speed should you generally travel at?
options: a:At the speed limit.,b:At a speed appropriate for road and weather conditions.,c:At the speed of vehicles surrounding you.
note: Drive at a speed appropriate for conditions. Never exceed the legal limit and reduce speed when conditions are poor.

question: If you must stop on the freeway shoulder because of an emergency, you should:
options: a:Leave the vehicle in the lane to block traffic.,b:Get out and walk along the roadway to find help.,c:Raise your vehicle's hood,d:Stand behind the car in traffic to warn others.
note: If stopped on the shoulder in an emergency, raise the hood and hazard lights to signal distress and remain in your vehicle if it is safe to do so.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing another vehicle, how do you know it's safe to return to your lane?
options: a:When you cannot see the vehicle directly to your right.,b:When you have passed the other vehicle's front bumper.,c:When you see the vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.
note: Only return to your lane after passing when you can see both of the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.

question: When driving behind another vehicle at night you should use:
options: a:Your low beam headlights.,b:High beams until you are within 10 feet of the vehicle ahead.,c:Hazard lights.,d:Fog lights only.
note: Use low beam headlights when following another vehicle closely to avoid glaring the driver ahead.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you want to enter the freeway but cannot find a gap, you should:
options: a:Stop at the end of the ramp and wait for traffic to clear.,b:Slow down on the ramp and wait for a gap.,c:Force your way into traffic since you are already on the ramp.,d:Reverse down the ramp to look for a gap.
note: If there is no suitable gap, reduce speed on the ramp and wait for a safe opening rather than stopping at the end or forcing entry.

question: What does a solid yellow arrow on a traffic signal mean?
options: a:You should speed up so you can make the turn before the light changes.,b:You should prepare to stop and yield the right-of-way to oncoming traffic.,c:You do not need to signal to turn from the indicated lane.
note: A solid yellow arrow means the protection of a green arrow is ending. Prepare to stop and yield to oncoming traffic before turning.

question: If a child is riding a bicycle near your vehicle you should:
options: a:Expect the unexpected and be prepared to react.,b:Speed past quickly to avoid them.,c:Sound your horn repeatedly to scare them away.,d:Assume the child will maintain perfect control.
note: Children on bicycles can behave unpredictably; be alert and prepared to stop or take evasive action.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an intersection controlled by a flashing yellow light you must:
options: a:Treat it as a flashing red light.,b:Stop and wait for a green light.,c:Slow down and cross the intersection carefully.,d:Turn on your hazard lights and proceed.
note: A flashing yellow light means to slow down and proceed with caution, watching for cross traffic and pedestrians.

question: As a vehicle's speed increases, stopping distances and crash severity generally:
options: a:Decrease.,b:Increase.,c:Vary only with the driver's skill.,d:Remain the same.
note: Higher speeds increase stopping distances and the potential severity of collisions; increase following distance accordingly.

question: After a minor collision at an intersection with no injuries, you should:
options: a:Leave your vehicle in the lane until police arrive.,b:Immediately drive away from the scene.,c:Move your vehicle out of the traffic lane if it is safe to do so.,d:Stand in traffic to direct other vehicles.
note: If no one is injured and the vehicle can be moved, you should remove it from the traffic lane to a safe location.

question: How should you place your hands to be able to turn quickly?
options: a:On the top and bottom of the steering wheel.,b:On opposite sides of the steering wheel.,c:Next to each other on the top of the steering wheel.
note: Both hands should be on opposite sides of the steering wheel to provide better control for turns.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If the intersection ahead is blocked by traffic while your light is green, what should you do?
options: a:Continue into the intersection and wait for traffic to clear.,b:Do not enter the intersection until you can get completely across.,c:Partially enter the intersection to establish your right-of-way.
note: You must not enter and block an intersection even if your light is green; wait until you can get completely through.

question: If you have consumed several alcoholic drinks, the impairing effects will be reduced only by:
options: a:Exercising vigorously.,b:Drinking coffee.,c:Taking a cold shower.,d:Waiting several hours.
note: Only time allows the body to metabolize alcohol and reduce impairment; other measures do not sober you up.

question: When driving on snowy or icy roads you should:
options: a:Use cruise control to maintain a steady speed.,b:Brake abruptly to stop quickly.,c:Drive exactly as you would on dry pavement.,d:Make speed and directional changes more gradually and avoid using cruise control.
note: On snow or ice, make gradual changes in speed and direction and avoid cruise control to reduce the risk of losing traction.

question: What does a yellow left-turn arrow indicate?
options: a:Drivers should prepare to yield to oncoming traffic.,b:The protected left turn is about to end.,c:Both of the above.
note: When a protected turn arrow changes from green to yellow, drivers must prepare to yield to oncoming traffic; the protected turn is ending.

question: Which statement is correct about using your feet for controls?
options: a:Always brake abruptly to ensure stopping.,b:Use either foot interchangeably for smoother control.,c:Use your right foot for both the brake and accelerator.,d:Use your left foot for braking.
note: Use your right foot for both accelerating and braking for consistent and safe control of the vehicle.

question: How should you drive on a dimly lit street at night?
options: a:Turn on your high beam headlights to better see the vehicles ahead of you.,b:Keep the instrument panel lights bright to be more visible to other drivers.,c:Drive slowly enough that you can stop within the area illuminated by your headlights.
note: At night, drive slowly enough to be able to stop within the area illuminated by your headlights.

question: A "No passing zone" sign informs drivers that:
options: a:It is not safe to pass in the indicated area.,b:You must maintain a steady speed.,c:Passing is permitted with caution.,d:You should speed up slightly and pass quickly.
note: No passing zone signs mark areas where passing other vehicles is unsafe and prohibited.

question: While in a vehicle on a highway, it is:
options: a:Illegal to possess or consume open containers of alcohol.,b:Legal to drink alcohol as a passenger.,c:Allowed to have open containers if you are not driving.,d:Permitted if sealed and unopened.
note: It is illegal to possess open containers or drink alcohol in a motor vehicle on a highway regardless of whether you are driving.

question: Why should you avoid using high beams in fog or mist?
options: a:Vehicles behind you may follow too closely.,b:Approaching vehicles might not see you.,c:The light will reflect back into your eyes.
note: In foggy or misty conditions, high beams reflect back and reduce visibility. Use low beams instead.

question: When is turning and stopping especially hazardous in rainy weather?
options: a:One half hour after it stops raining.,b:After it has been raining all day.,c:During the first half hour of rain.
note: Be extra careful during the first half hour of rain because oil on the pavement can mix with water and create slippery conditions.

question: Which of these is correct about railroad crossings?
options: a:You have the right-of-way at a railroad crossing and do not need to stop.,b:You should put on your cruise control near a railroad crossing to maintain a constant speed.,c:You must stop at a railroad crossing when directed to do so by a flagger or stop sign.
note: You must stop at a railroad crossing when directed to do so by a flagger, stop sign, or warning signal. Use caution when driving near railroad tracks.

question: What should you do when the roadway is wet or icy?
options: a:Speed up.,b:Drive at the posted speed.,c:Reduce your speed.
note: Because tires have less grip in wet, snowy, or icy conditions, you should slow down until conditions improve.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When driving beside a single broken white line, what does it mean?
options: a:You may only cross the line to change lanes if you are in the left lane.,b:You cannot cross the line to pass.,c:You may cross the line to pass and change lanes.
note: White lines separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction. You may cross a dashed white line to pass or change lanes if safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a flashing red traffic signal you must:
options: a:Slow down and go through if no other vehicles are present.,b:Come to a complete stop,c:Yield only to traffic on your left.,d:Treat it the same as a flashing yellow.
note: A flashing red signal means stop; then yield to any other traffic or pedestrians before proceeding.

question: Which substances can impair your ability to drive?
options: a:All of the above.,b:Cough syrups and cold tablets containing codeine or antihistamines.,c:Tranquilizers
note: Many drugs can impair driving, including prescription depressants, over-the-counter cough medicines, and illegal drugs.

question: When are streets and highways most slippery?
options: a:Just after it starts to rain.,b:When they are clean and dry.,c:When it has been raining hard for several hours.
note: Roadways are especially slippery just after rain begins because oil and chemicals on the surface mix with water.

question: At dawn, dusk, or in rain and snow you should turn on:
options: a:Only your parking lights.,b:Your headlights.,c:Your high beam lights.,d:Your interior instrument lights.
note: Use headlights when visibility is reduced so other drivers can see you; use low beams if weather requires windshield wipers.

question: If you see a pedestrian using a guide dog or white cane, you must:
options: a:Sound your horn and pass quickly.,b:Proceed if they are not in a crosswalk.,c:Ask them to move to the curb.,d:Yield the right-of-way to that pedestrian.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians who use a guide dog or white cane; they have the right-of-way.

question: What is a major risk associated with excessive speed?
options: a:Saves time so you can get to your destination more quickly.,b:Helps you maneuver around obstacles.,c:It increases the likelihood of serious bodily injury and death.
note: Excessive speed is a common contributing factor in crashes and greatly increases the severity of injuries.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When crossing a sidewalk to enter traffic from an alley or driveway, what should drivers do?
options: a:Stop only if pedestrians are on the sidewalk.,b:Stop before driving onto the sidewalk or sidewalk area.,c:Expect pedestrians to yield the right-of-way.
note: When leaving an alley, driveway, or parking lot, stop before driving onto the sidewalk. Pedestrians have the right-of-way.

question: To reduce the chance of skidding on slippery surfaces, what should you do before curves and intersections?
options: a:Speed up to enter curves and slow down to exit them.,b:Shift to a lower gear after starting down a steep hill.,c:Slow down before entering curves and intersections.
note: Slow down before you enter a curve or intersection. Braking on a curve may cause a skid.

question: If you see animals standing near the roadway, what should you do?
options: a:Stop in the traffic lane and wait.,b:Speed up to scare them away.,c:Quickly swerve into the next lane.,d:Slow down and proceed with caution.
note: Animals may suddenly move into the roadway; slow down and be prepared to stop or take evasive action safely.

question: If you must park somewhere not normally used for parking, what should you do?
options: a:Park five feet from the curb.,b:Park with your reverse lights on.,c:Make sure your vehicle is visible to drivers approaching from any direction.
note: Drivers must ensure parked vehicles do not become hazards. Wherever you park, make sure your car is visible to approaching drivers.

question: If the rear of your vehicle is skidding to the left, how should you steer?
options: a:Not turn your steering wheel.,b:Turn your steering wheel to the left to correct the skid.,c:Turn your steering wheel to the right to correct the skid.
note: If you skid, take your foot off the accelerator, avoid the brakes, and steer in the direction of the skid unless you have ABS and need to brake firmly.

question: If you become drowsy while driving, the safest option is to:
options: a:Turn on the air conditioning and keep driving.,b:Open the windows and play loud music.,c:Drink coffee and continue driving.,d:Stop to rest or change drivers.
note: Stopping and resting or switching drivers are the only safe ways to address dangerous drowsiness while driving.

question: Which of these is a safe driving technique?
options: a:Keeping both hands off the wheel while steering.,b:Checking your rearview mirrors frequently.,c:Using high beams in heavy fog.,d:Staring fixedly at the point directly ahead of your vehicle.
note: Regularly checking mirrors helps you stay aware of surrounding traffic and hazards; high beams in fog reduce visibility.

question: If the rear of your car begins to skid to the left, you should:
options: a:Steer to the left (in the direction of the skid).,b:Steer to the right (away from the skid).,c:Turn off the engine immediately.,d:Tap the brakes hard and shift to neutral.
note: When the rear end skids left, steer left to align the front and rear of the vehicle and regain control.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you check your blind spot before changing lanes?
options: a:Use your side mirror only.,b:Use the inside rearview mirror.,c:Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
note: Mirrors don't show all areas. Turn your head and look over your shoulder to check blind spots before changing lanes.

question: When passing a motorcycle, you must:
options: a:Return to the right lane immediately after the motorcycle starts to speed up.,b:Move completely into the left lane so the motorcycle has a full lane.,c:Sound your horn and pass closely.,d:Pass within the same lane to save time.
note: Give a motorcycle a full lane when passing; do not share a lane with a motorcycle and make sure you are entirely in the left lane while passing.

question: The first ability affected by alcohol is typically:
options: a:Coordination.,b:Judgment.,c:Vision.,d:Balance.
note: Alcohol first impairs judgment and decision-making, which then leads to other driving errors.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering traffic from a parked position at a curb, you should:
options: a:Enter at any time because you have the right-of-way.,b:Drive more slowly than traffic for the first 200 feet.,c:Wait for a gap large enough for your vehicle to get up to the speed of traffic.,d:Wait for two vehicles to pass and then go.
note: Only merge into traffic when there is a gap sufficient for your vehicle to accelerate to the flow of traffic.

question: If your vehicle begins to skid, you should:
options: a:Shift into neutral and speed up.,b:Turn off the ignition to regain control.,c:Brake hard immediately.,d:Ease off the gas pedal and steer in the direction you want to go.
note: If skidding, release the accelerator, avoid heavy braking, and steer toward the direction you want the vehicle to go to regain control.

question: Which best describes a driving distraction?
options: a:Anything that causes you to pay more attention to driving.,b:Anything that takes your attention away from driving.,c:Anything that causes evasive action while driving.
note: A distraction when driving is anything that takes your attention away from driving. Distracted driving can lead to collisions, injuries, and death.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should a driver approach right-of-way decisions?
options: a:Assume most drivers obey the right-of-way rules.,b:Assume all drivers automatically obey the right-of-way rules.,c:Always be prepared to yield the right-of-way.
note: Do not assume you automatically have the right-of-way. Be prepared to yield if it will prevent a collision.

question: A blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of 0.02 percent is associated with what change in crash risk?
options: a:Is legal and safe to drive.,b:Reduces risk slightly.,c:Has no effect on driving ability.,d:Nearly doubles your chance of having an accident.
note: Even low BAC levels (like 0.02%) significantly increase the risk of a crash compared to sober driving.

question: What are "No zones" around large trucks?
options: a:Zones where trucks must stop.,b:Loading zones for trucks only.,c:Areas where cars disappear into blind spots or are too close for the truck to maneuver safely.,d:Areas where it is safest to drive next to a truck.
note: No zones are the large blind spot areas around trucks where cars can be hidden from the truck driver's view or too close to allow safe maneuvers.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you yield your legal right-of-way?
options: a:Never; always insist on your right-of-way.,b:Only when the other driver signals.,c:Whenever yielding helps prevent a collision.,d:Only at uncontrolled intersections.
note: Yield your right-of-way whenever doing so will prevent a crash; never assume others will yield.

question: What does Georgia's Implied Consent Law require?
options: a:You agree to be tested for alcohol or drugs if arrested for drunk or impaired driving.,b:You must sign a statement saying you won't drive after drinking more than three drinks.,c:You consent to have a blood sample taken if an officer stops you for driving recklessly.
note: Georgia's Implied Consent Law requires submitting to state-administered chemical tests when requested by law enforcement; refusal results in suspension.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If another vehicle is passing you in a no-passing zone, you should:
options: a:Pull off the road.,b:Slow down and allow the passing vehicle to return to the travel lane safely.,c:Speed up to prevent them from passing.,d:Flash your lights angrily.
note: If someone is passing in a no-passing area, reduce speed and allow them to return safely to the lane when possible.

question: If you start to get tired while driving, what should you do?
options: a:Stop and either get rest or change drivers.,b:Open a window to stay alert.,c:Drink something with caffeine.
note: To avoid the dangers of fatigued driving, take regular breaks or change drivers. Caffeine is not a substitute for rest.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Why should you look farther ahead on a freeway than on a city street?
options: a:Because it takes a quarter of a mile to stop your vehicle completely.,b:Because it helps you keep up with traffic.,c:In order to see potential hazards early.
note: On freeways, look farther ahead to spot hazards early, anticipate merging traffic, and respond to rapid changes in flow.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At what speed should you be traveling when merging onto the freeway?
options: a:Five to 10 mph slower than the speed of traffic.,b:The posted speed limit for freeway traffic.,c:At or near the speed of traffic on the freeway.
note: When merging, enter at or near the speed of traffic so you can safely blend into the traffic flow.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To help vehicles entering the freeway, you should:
options: a:Maintain your exact speed and position always.,b:Increase your speed so they cannot merge.,c:Stop in your lane to allow them to enter.,d:Change lanes or slow down to create a gap
note: Make space by merging or adjusting speed when safe so vehicles can enter the freeway smoothly.

question: What does a diamond-shaped road sign indicate?
options: a:Yield.,b:Stop.,c:Warning.
note: Diamond-shaped signs warn drivers of special conditions or hazards ahead and are typically yellow or orange.

question: If your vehicle has a two-part seat belt system, how should you wear it?
options: a:Use both the lap and shoulder belts.,b:Use only the shoulder belt.,c:Use only the lap belt.
note: If your vehicle has a lap-and-shoulder belt, be sure to wear both. Wearing only one part greatly reduces protection.

question: If someone is injured in an accident you are involved in, one immediate requirement is to:
options: a:Leave the scene and seek help elsewhere.,b:Render aid to the injured.,c:Only call the other driver's family.,d:Notify your insurance agent before assisting.
note: Provide aid to injured persons and summon professional help as soon as possible; do not assume no one is injured.

question: When double solid yellow lines separate lanes, what is true?
options: a:Passing is permitted from the left only.,b:Passing is permitted from the right only.,c:You may cross to pass if traffic is light.,d:Passing is not permitted from either direction.
note: Double solid yellow lines indicate no passing by vehicles traveling in either direction.

question: A broken yellow centerline indicates:
options: a:Passing on the right is always permitted.,b:Traffic flows in the same direction on both sides.,c:Passing is never permitted.,d:Passing on the left is permitted when the way ahead is clear.
note: A broken yellow centerline on your side means you may cross to pass when it is safe to do so; it separates opposing traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the maximum speed limit on a rural interstate in Georgia unless posted otherwise?
options: a:60 miles per hour.,b:70 miles per hour.,c:65 miles per hour.,d:55 miles per hour.
note: The maximum speed on a rural interstate in Georgia is 70 mph unless signs indicate a different limit.

question: Signs with orange backgrounds are used to indicate:
options: a:School zones.,b:Construction and maintenance warnings.,c:General regulatory messages.,d:Motorist services.
note: Orange signs specifically warn drivers of construction and maintenance activities in the area.

question: When you approach an octagonal sign, what must you do?
options: a:Slow.,b:Turn.,c:Stop.
note: An octagonal (eight-sided) sign always means "Stop." Come to a complete stop, yield, and proceed when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a dashed yellow line next to a solid yellow line mean on a multilane road?
options: a:Passing is permitted only from the direction next to the dashed line.,b:Passing is permitted from both directions.,c:Passing is prohibited from both directions.
note: Where solid and dashed yellow lines separate lanes, only traffic next to the dashed line may cross to pass.

question: If there is a deep puddle on the road ahead you should:
options: a:Avoid the puddle if possible.,b:Shift into neutral while driving through it.,c:Maintain posted speed to drive through it.,d:Increase your speed slightly.
note: Avoid deep puddles when possible to prevent loss of control or damage; slow down and detour if safe to do so.

question: As daylight begins to fade, which lights should you use to help others see you?
options: a:Parking lights.,b:Emergency flashers.,c:Low beam headlights.
note: Turn on low beams as daylight fades. Use high beams only where no other drivers are present.

question: If the road is slippery you should maintain a following distance that is:
options: a:Closer than normal.,b:Farther than normal.,c:The minimum legal distance.,d:The same as normal.
note: Slippery conditions increase stopping distance; maintain a greater following gap than usual.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: As you enter a roundabout, you should:
options: a:Yield to pedestrians and bicyclists and to any traffic already in the roundabout.,b:Enter quickly without yielding.,c:Stop before entering even if there is no traffic.,d:Signal left and pass other vehicles inside the roundabout.
note: When entering a roundabout, yield to pedestrians and bicyclists and to drivers already circulating in the roundabout.

question: Which statement about alcohol and driving is correct?
options: a:If you can walk in a straight line after drinking,b:If you are under the legal blood alcohol concentration limit,c:Alcohol affects judgment
note: Alcohol impairs judgment, which is essential for safe driving. Even small amounts can affect your ability to drive safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a broken yellow centerline indicate?
options: a:Passing on the right is permitted when the way ahead is clear.,b:Passing on the left is permitted when the way ahead is clear.,c:Passing is not permitted.
note: A broken yellow centerline allows drivers to cross to pass another vehicle on the left if there is no oncoming traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parking downhill on a two-way road with no curb, which way should you turn your front wheels?
options: a:Toward the center of the road (left).,b:Toward the nearest driveway.,c:Toward the side of the road (right).,d:Straight ahead.
note: When parking downhill with no curb, turn the wheels toward the edge of the road so the vehicle will roll away from traffic if it moves.

question: What type of information do blue road signs provide?
options: a:Motorist services (such as rest areas and hospitals).,b:Mileage distances to specific locations.,c:Construction and maintenance information.
note: Blue signs are service signs providing information about motorist services like rest areas, food, or hospitals.

question: Blue roadway signs are used to give drivers information about:
options: a:Construction and maintenance.,b:Motorist services such as rest areas and hospitals.,c:Regulatory requirements.,d:School zones.
note: Blue signs are service signs that provide information about facilities and services available to motorists.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a freeway, how should you check traffic before merging?
options: a:Using your rearview mirror only.,b:Using your rearview and side mirrors only.,c:Using your side mirror and looking over your shoulder.
note: Use side mirrors and a shoulder check to see and anticipate traffic when entering a freeway.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering the interstate from a short ramp with no acceleration lane, what is the correct action?
options: a:Speed up and enter only after you have identified a gap in traffic.,b:Use the shoulder of the main road to get up to the speed of traffic.,c:Immediately enter the far-right lane and speed up to match traffic.
note: When there is no acceleration lane, do not merge until you find a safe gap in traffic; often you may need to stop and wait for a gap.

question: If a tire suddenly blows out while you are driving, what is the proper response?
options: a:Grip the steering wheel firmly, slow down, and exit the traffic lane.,b:Pump the brakes rapidly.,c:Brake hard and steer toward the right edge of the roadway.
note: If a tire blows out, remain calm, grasp the wheel firmly, ease off the accelerator, slow gradually, and move safely out of traffic.

question: What color are construction and maintenance traffic devices?
options: a:Orange.,b:Yellow.,c:Red.
note: Orange warning signs are used in and around work zones. Use special caution when you see orange signs, cones, or barriers.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should the maximum posted speed limit be considered appropriate?
options: a:During the night.,b:During the day.,c:Only under ideal conditions.
note: The posted maximum speed is the fastest legal speed under ideal conditions. Adjust speed for traffic, weather, and road conditions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the likely result of driving slower than the flow of traffic?
options: a:You will most likely interfere with traffic and may receive a ticket.,b:You will demonstrate defensive driving techniques.,c:You will improve traffic flow.
note: Driving significantly slower than surrounding traffic can block traffic flow and may result in a citation.

question: When a large truck is turning right on a multi-lane street, it may:
options: a:Be unable to make the turn without reversing.,b:Need to swing wide to complete the turn.,c:Turn only from the left lane.,d:Always stay in the right lane and turn tightly.
note: Large trucks often swing wide during right turns because their rear wheels follow a shorter path than the front wheels.

question: If a truck or bus is making a right turn and you also need to turn right, what should you do?
options: a:Wait until the truck or bus completes its turn before you turn.,b:Squeeze between the truck or bus and the curb.,c:Quickly turn before the truck or bus is able to.
note: Do not attempt to insert your vehicle between a large vehicle and the curb while it turns. Wait until it completes the turn.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a four-way stop, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The driver who signals first.,b:The driver across from you.,c:The driver who arrived before you.,d:The driver on your left.
note: Proceed in the order vehicles arrive; if multiple vehicles arrive simultaneously, yield to the vehicle on your right.

question: A solid yellow line next to a broken yellow line means:
options: a:Drivers next to the broken line may pass when safe.,b:No passing is permitted in either direction.,c:Passing is permitted for both directions.,d:Drivers next to the solid line may pass when safe.
note: When a broken yellow line is beside a solid yellow line, traffic adjacent to the broken line may pass when it is safe; the side next to the solid line may not pass.

question: Which statement about drugs and driving is correct?
options: a:Any prescription drug is safe to use if you don't feel drowsy.,b:Only illegal drugs can impair your driving.,c:Even over-the-counter drugs can impair your driving.
note: Prescription and over-the-counter drugs can impair driving. It is illegal to drive while impaired by any drug.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto an interstate highway you should:
options: a:Merge across two lanes at once to save time.,b:Always stop on the ramp and wait for an opening.,c:Turn on hazard lights while merging.,d:Select a safe gap and merge into the traffic lane.
note: Identify a gap, accelerate to match traffic speed, signal, and merge safely into the chosen lane.

question: When should you adjust your rearview and side mirrors?
options: a:After you begin driving.,b:While the vehicle is moving at low speed.,c:Before you start driving.,d:Only when another driver asks you to.
note: Adjust mirrors before moving so you have proper visibility; do not adjust them while the vehicle is in motion.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which is required for safe interstate driving?
options: a:Be constantly alert.,b:Both a and b.,c:Be able to safely drive at higher speeds.,d:Only use cruise control at all times.
note: Driving on the interstate requires both heightened alertness and the ability to operate safely at higher speeds.

question: What is the purpose of rumble strips?
options: a:They test a vehicle's shock absorbers.,b:They alert drivers to potential tire problems.,c:Through vibration and sound
note: Rumble strips create noise and vibration to warn drowsy or inattentive drivers that they are straying from the travel lane.

question: When parking uphill on a street with a curb, how should you set your wheels?
options: a:Leave the front wheels straight.,b:Turn the front wheels away from the curb.,c:Turn the front wheels toward the curb.
note: When parking uphill with a curb, turn the wheels away from the curb so the vehicle will roll away from traffic if it moves.

question: When a bicyclist is preparing to turn left, what may you expect?
options: a:They must cut across all lanes diagonally.,b:They will always stay far to the right.,c:They may use the left lane to complete their turn.,d:They must always dismount and walk their bicycle.
note: Bicyclists making a left turn may use the left lane or behave as a vehicle would to complete the turn; drivers should anticipate this.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Who must drivers obey when directing traffic at a construction site?
options: a:Other drivers whose vehicles are broken down on the roadway.,b:Security guards patrolling parking lots.,c:Flaggers (signal persons) at construction sites.
note: Drivers must obey signs or instructions given by flaggers to keep drivers and workers safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parking uphill on a two-way road with no curb, which way do you turn your front wheels?
options: a:Toward the side of the road (right).,b:Toward the center of the road (left).,c:Toward the nearest driveway.,d:Straight ahead.
note: When parked uphill without a curb, turn the wheels so the vehicle will roll away from the center of the road if the brakes fail.

question: When poor visibility due to bad weather limits what you can see, what should you do?
options: a:Speed up to get off the road quickly.,b:Drive in the lane closest to oncoming traffic.,c:Increase your following distance.
note: When visibility is reduced, increase following distance to give yourself more time to react to hazards you may not see in advance.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: From which lane should you begin a left turn from a multilane one-way street onto another one-way street?
options: a:Any lane (as long as it is safe).,b:The lane in the center of the road.,c:The lane closest to the left curb.
note: When turning left from a one-way street onto another one-way street, begin the turn from the far left lane.

question: When passing a row of parked cars, what should you be prepared for?
options: a:Driving closely to the parked vehicles to allow more room for traffic.,b:Someone or a vehicle suddenly entering your lane.,c:Expecting all other drivers and pedestrians to respect your right-of-way.
note: Keep space between your vehicle and parked cars; a person or another vehicle may unexpectedly enter your lane.

question: The measurement of alcohol in a person's blood is called:
options: a:Blood alcohol concentration (BAC).,b:Rate of alcohol consumption (RAC).,c:Implied consent (IC).,d:Alcohol blood level (ABL).
note: BAC measures the percentage of alcohol in the bloodstream and indicates level of impairment.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Facing a green light but the intersection ahead is blocked by traffic, you should:
options: a:Enter the intersection and block it until cars move.,b:Proceed if you can squeeze through.,c:Stay out of the intersection until the traffic ahead clears.,d:Make a U-turn to find another route.
note: Do not enter an intersection unless you can clear it completely; blocking an intersection can result in a citation.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Approaching an intersection with a flashing yellow light, you should:
options: a:Stop before crossing.,b:Speed up to clear the intersection quickly.,c:Slow down and proceed with caution.,d:Wait for green before going.
note: A flashing yellow light means slow down and proceed with caution after checking for hazards.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After passing another vehicle, when is it safe to return to your lane?
options: a:When the driver you passed signals you to move over.,b:After three seconds have passed.,c:When you can see the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.,d:When you are halfway past the vehicle.
note: Only return to your lane when you can see the passed vehicle’s headlights in your rearview mirror, indicating you have a safe distance.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you encounter a steady yellow traffic signal and you have not entered the intersection, you should:
options: a:Speed up to beat the red light.,b:Proceed only if turning right.,c:Continue at the same speed no matter what.,d:Come to a safe stop.
note: A steady yellow indicates the light will soon turn red; you should stop safely if you have not entered the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: In which situation should your wheels NOT be pointed straight ahead?
options: a:When parked on a hill or sloping driveway.,b:When waiting to make a left turn at a traffic light.,c:When passing another car.,d:When stopped at a red light on level ground.
note: When parked on a slope, turn the wheels so the vehicle will not roll into traffic if the brakes fail; when waiting to turn left, keep wheels straight until you begin the turn.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are in an intersection and an emergency vehicle is approaching with lights and siren, you should:
options: a:Immediately stop in the intersection and wait.,b:Stop and block the intersection.,c:Continue through the intersection,d:Speed up and try to outrun it.
note: If you are in the intersection when an emergency vehicle approaches, clear the intersection then pull to the right and stop to yield the right-of-way.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following is unlawful regarding passing?
options: a:Passing on a two-lane road when indicated by a broken centerline.,b:Passing if the vehicle ahead signals you to pass.,c:Passing only when the way is clear.,d:Passing in a marked no-passing zone or over a railroad crossing.
note: You may not pass in marked no-passing zones, at railroad crossings, on hills or curves where you cannot see ahead, or where a solid yellow line forbids it.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On public roadways, bicycles are legally classified as:
options: a:Vehicles.,b:Objects.,c:Pedestrians.,d:Hazards.
note: When bicycles are ridden on public roadways they are considered vehicles and cyclists must obey the same rules of the road as motor vehicles.

question: What does a curb painted red mean?
options: a:No parking,b:The area is reserved for picking up or dropping off passengers.,c:Loading zone.
note: You may not stop, stand, or park at a curb painted red.

question: After which activity is reaction time slower?
options: a:Sleeping.,b:Working hard.,c:Drinking alcohol.
note: Alcohol slows reflexes and reaction time, reducing alertness and impairing driving ability.

question: If a tire blows out, which is the proper procedure?
options: a:Apply the brake and hold it firmly.,b:Pull over quickly without slowing down.,c:Hold the steering wheel tightly and use the brakes lightly.
note: If a tire suddenly blows out, keep the vehicle straight, slow gradually by easing off the gas, and use the brakes lightly when safe.

question: If your wheels drop off the paved roadway onto the shoulder, what should you do?
options: a:Reduce speed,b:Speed up and re-enter quickly.,c:Turn sharply back onto the roadway immediately.,d:Stop immediately where you are.
note: If your wheels leave the pavement, slow down, check traffic, and re-enter the roadway gradually when it is safe to do so; do not swerve back onto the road abruptly.

question: If you become drowsy while driving, what is the recommended action?
options: a:Try to fight it.,b:Take some caffeine pills.,c:Take a break.
note: If you start to feel tired, drive to the first safe rest stop to take a break or change drivers. Caffeine pills are not a substitute for rest.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you see pedestrians near the roadway, what is the proper action?
options: a:Drive on the shoulder to give them more room.,b:Speed up to clear the area quickly.,c:Sound your horn and maintain speed.,d:Slow down and pass with caution.
note: Slow down and be prepared to stop for pedestrians near the road; drive cautiously through the area.

question: How should you respond when confronted by an aggressive driver?
options: a:Challenge them.,b:Get out of their way.,c:Speed up to escape them.
note: When encountering an aggressive driver, it is safest to move out of their way and avoid engaging or competing with them.

question: Which behavior may indicate someone is driving aggressively?
options: a:Erratic and improper lane changes.,b:Their tendency to drive slowly.,c:The number of passengers in their car.
note: Aggressive drivers often make erratic or improper lane changes. If you notice this, avoid challenging them.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After passing on the left, when may you safely move back into the right lane?
options: a:When the passed driver waves you back.,b:When you can see the front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,c:When you are directly alongside the passed vehicle.,d:After three seconds have elapsed.
note: Only return to the right lane when you can see the passed vehicle’s front in your rearview mirror, indicating sufficient space.

question: If you are near a large commercial vehicle you should:
options: a:Avoid driving beside it for long stretches of time.,b:Signal aggressively to get ahead.,c:Follow closely to reduce wind drag.,d:Drive on its right side on curves and hills.
note: Large commercial vehicles have big blind spots; avoid lingering alongside them where the driver cannot see you.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before entering an intersection you should look:
options: a:Only to the right.,b:Left,c:Only to the left.,d:Down the road only.
note: Look left, then right, then left again before entering to ensure no vehicles or pedestrians are approaching from any direction.

question: If there is no crosswalk and a pedestrian is crossing your lane, what should you do?
options: a:Make sure the pedestrian can see you before proceeding.,b:Cautiously drive around the pedestrian.,c:Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing.
note: Drivers must yield the right-of-way to pedestrians in the roadway, even if there is no marked crosswalk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you see pedestrians in a crosswalk ahead, what must you do?
options: a:Continue because you have the right-of-way.,b:Drive around them on the right if there is room.,c:Flash your headlights and proceed.,d:Wait for the pedestrians to finish crossing.
note: Drivers must yield the right-of-way to pedestrians who are within a crosswalk and wait until the crosswalk is clear before proceeding.

question: When should you increase the distance between your vehicle and the one ahead?
options: a:When you are driving more slowly than the posted speed limit.,b:When you are following a small passenger vehicle.,c:When you are being tailgated by another driver.
note: If you are being tailgated, create extra space in front of your vehicle and avoid sudden braking to reduce collision risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A flashing red traffic light at an intersection means:
options: a:Proceed with caution without stopping.,b:The light will soon turn green.,c:The same as a stop sign — come to a complete stop.,d:The same as a yield sign.
note: A flashing red light requires a full stop and yielding to other traffic and pedestrians, just like a stop sign.

question: Which statement about driving and taking medications is true?
options: a:Prescription medicines never impair driving.,b:Many over-the-counter cold medicines can make you drowsy.,c:Medications are safe to use while driving if taken with coffee.,d:All over-the-counter medications are safe for driving.
note: Over-the-counter and prescription medicines can impair driving; many cold and allergy medicines cause drowsiness.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under what circumstances may you legally block an intersection?
options: a:During rush hour traffic.,b:Under no circumstances.,c:If you entered the intersection on a green light.
note: Even if the light is green, do not enter an intersection unless you can get completely across before the light turns red.

question: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means:
options: a:Traffic next to the broken line may pass,b:The lane next to the solid line may pass anytime.,c:Neither lane may pass.,d:Both lanes may pass.
note: The lane adjacent to the broken line is permitted to pass when safe; the lane next to the solid line is not.

question: If you hit a parked car and cannot find the owner, what must you do?
options: a:Wait for the owner to return.,b:Leave a note with your name and address on the parked vehicle.,c:Call your insurance company when you get home.
note: If you hit a parked vehicle or property, leave a note with your name, phone number, and address securely attached to the vehicle or property.

question: Which statement about roadwork zones is correct?
options: a:Fines are always the same as in normal traffic.,b:Only slow down if workers are present.,c:You must slow down in work zones (Slow for the Cone Zone).,d:You may pass workers closely if traffic is light.
note: Reduce speed and exercise caution in work zones to protect workers and other road users; fines are often increased in these zones.

question: Which statement about blind spots is correct?
options: a:Motorcycles have no blind spots.,b:You can always see blind spots in your rearview mirrors.,c:Blind spots are eliminated if you have one outside mirror on each side.,d:Large trucks have larger blind spots than most passenger vehicles.
note: Blind spots are areas not visible in mirrors; large trucks have particularly large blind spots that other drivers should avoid.

question: If a tire suddenly goes flat while driving you should:
options: a:Brake hard immediately to stop quickly.,b:Rapidly pump the brake pedal several times.,c:Grip the steering wheel,d:Turn sharply off the road.
note: If a tire blows out, hold the wheel firmly, reduce speed gradually, avoid sudden braking, and pull off the road when safe.

question: At a railroad crossing you must:
options: a:Watch for vehicles that must stop at all crossings and for multiple trains.,b:Ignore crossings if you do not see flashing lights.,c:Always cross immediately without stopping.,d:Assume only one train can approach at a time.
note: Approach crossings with caution, be aware of vehicles like school buses that must stop, and watch for more than one train.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To view objects in a blind spot when changing lanes, what should you do?
options: a:Only check the left outside mirror.,b:Only check the inside rearview mirror.,c:Look over your left or right shoulder.
note: Blind spots are not visible in mirrors. Look over the appropriate shoulder to check before changing lanes.

question: When changing lanes, you should do which of the following?
options: a:Look over your shoulder toward the direction you plan to move.,b:Change lanes without looking if you have signaled.,c:Rely only on your rearview mirror.,d:Rely only on the side mirror on the direction you're moving toward.
note: Always glance over your shoulder to check blind spots before changing lanes in addition to using mirrors and signals.

question: If a child is about to run into the street, what should you do?
options: a:Flash your headlights at them.,b:Slow down slightly but keep moving.,c:Speed up to pass before they run out.,d:Sound a sharp blast of your horn and be prepared to stop.
note: If a child is about to enter the roadway, a sharp horn blast can warn them and help prevent a crash; be prepared to stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a police officer directs you to go through a red light without stopping, what should you do?
options: a:Come to a complete stop before proceeding.,b:Follow the officer's directions and go through the intersection.,c:Stop until the light turns green.
note: Instructions from police officers directing traffic override posted traffic signals and signs. Always follow the officer's directions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following is NOT a safe practice on an interstate?
options: a:Signaling before lane changes.,b:Changing lanes without signaling.,c:Slower traffic keeping to the right.,d:If you miss an exit
note: Failing to signal before changing lanes is unsafe and illegal; always use signals when changing lanes.

question: When is it appropriate to use your horn?
options: a:When it may help prevent a collision.,b:When another vehicle is in your way.,c:When another driver makes a mistake.
note: Only use your horn when necessary to avoid collisions. Do not use it to express frustration or to make others go faster.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A flashing yellow traffic signal at an intersection indicates you should:
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution.,b:Treat it as a green light.,c:Come to a complete stop.,d:Turn on your hazard lights.
note: A flashing yellow light requires you to slow down, be alert, and proceed through the intersection with caution.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the correct method to enter an expressway from an entrance ramp?
options: a:Go down the ramp and cross over to your desired traffic lane as soon as possible.,b:Use the acceleration lane to blend into traffic.,c:Go down to the bottom of the ramp and come to a complete stop before entering the expressway.
note: After entering the entrance ramp, move into the acceleration lane to adjust your speed to expressway traffic and merge safely.

question: If it feels like your tires have lost contact with the road surface, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down by pumping the brakes quickly and firmly.,b:Ease your foot off the gas pedal.,c:Slow down by shifting into a lower gear.
note: If your tires lose contact, ease off the accelerator and avoid braking or turning until traction returns.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What do double solid yellow lines down the center of the road indicate about passing?
options: a:Allowed from both directions.,b:Passing is not allowed from either direction.,c:Allowed only from your direction of travel.
note: A double solid yellow centerline indicates traffic in opposite directions and prohibits passing from either direction.

question: When a school bus is loading or unloading children, what must you do?
options: a:Stop,b:Slow down and be prepared to stop.,c:Stop only if you are driving in the same direction.
note: When a school bus is picking up or dropping off passengers, you must come to a complete stop regardless of your travel direction.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it permissible to pass another vehicle?
options: a:When you are on a road with a broken line next to your lane.,b:When you are on a road with a solid line next to your lane.,c:When you are on a hill or curve.
note: A single broken line indicates that drivers may cross from either lane to change lanes. Only change lanes when it is safe to do so.

question: Consistently looking far ahead while driving primarily helps to:
options: a:Find police officers more easily.,b:Maintain a constant speed regardless of conditions.,c:Make lane changes automatically.,d:Reduce the need for last-second braking or turning.
note: Scanning far ahead helps you anticipate hazards and reduces the need for sudden braking or evasive maneuvers.

question: If you see orange construction signs and cones on a freeway, what must you do?
options: a:Slow down because the lane ends ahead.,b:Be prepared for workers and equipment ahead.,c:Change lanes and maintain your current speed.
note: As you enter a work zone, signs warn you of workers and equipment. Reduce speed and be prepared to slow or stop.

question: A five-sided (pentagon) roadway sign is used to indicate:
options: a:A regulatory sign only.,b:A railroad crossing.,c:A school zone or school crossing.,d:A stop sign.
note: Pentagonal signs are used to warn drivers of school zones and school crossings where children may be present.

question: How should you drive in work zones regarding spacing?
options: a:Follow the driver in front of you closely.,b:Pass the driver in front of you as soon as you can.,c:Avoid tailgating and keep a safe following distance.
note: In work zones, increase following distance and avoid tailgating to protect workers and equipment.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto the interstate, you should:
options: a:Expect other drivers to always let you in.,b:Check for a gap,c:Merge across two lanes at once to find the fastest route.,d:Always stop at the end of the ramp before entering.
note: Accelerate to match traffic speed, signal, identify a gap, and merge carefully; do not assume others will yield.

question: If you parallel park facing downhill, how should you turn your wheels?
options: a:Turn your wheels away from the side of the road.,b:Keep your wheels straight.,c:Turn your wheels sharply toward the side of the road.
note: When parking downhill, turn your front wheels toward the curb or edge of the road so the vehicle will roll into the curb if it moves.

question: Driving while impaired by medication is allowed:
options: a:Only on short trips.,b:If you feel alert enough.,c:Under no circumstances.,d:If your doctor prescribed it.
note: It is illegal to drive under the influence of any medication that impairs your ability to drive safely, regardless of its source.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If your view at an intersection is blocked to the side, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down and look both ways.,b:Maintain your speed and look both ways.,c:Stop
note: If a clear view of cross traffic is obscured, stop and inch forward until you can see clearly in both directions.

question: To reduce the risk of hydroplaning in heavy rain you should:
options: a:Move to the shoulder immediately.,b:Use cruise control to maintain steady speed.,c:Decrease your speed.,d:Shift into neutral while driving through water.
note: Lowering speed in wet conditions reduces the chance tires will ride on water and lose contact with the road.

question: Why should you leave extra space in front of a large truck?
options: a:So you can use the space to stop quickly.,b:Because trucks require more distance to stop.,c:To reduce the truck's fuel consumption.,d:To allow the truck to pull off the road.
note: Large trucks need more distance to stop than cars; leaving extra space gives both vehicles room to react safely.

question: An orange and red triangular emblem displayed on the back of a vehicle means:
options: a:The vehicle has the right-of-way.,b:The vehicle is an emergency vehicle.,c:There is roadwork ahead.,d:The vehicle is a slow-moving vehicle.
note: An orange-red triangle indicates a slow-moving vehicle such as farm equipment or animal-drawn carts.

question: Which is a dangerous habit when driving in work zones?
options: a:Tailgating another vehicle.,b:Failing to carefully watch for workers and moving equipment.,c:Both tailgating another vehicle and failing to watch for workers and equipment.
note: Adjust your speed and be attentive in work zones; tailgating and failing to watch for workers are both dangerous.

question: If pedestrians are illegally crossing in the middle of the street, you:
options: a:Should honk and proceed.,b:Do not have to stop for them.,c:May drive around them aggressively.,d:Must still yield and stop for them.
note: Even if pedestrians are crossing illegally, drivers must yield and avoid hitting them by stopping if necessary.

question: You should leave extra following distance when you are behind:
options: a:Motor vehicles.,b:Station wagons.,c:Motorcycles.,d:Tractors only.
note: Allow extra space when following motorcycles because they can stop more quickly and are harder to see.

question: Why is driving at night more dangerous than daytime driving?
options: a:Your vehicle handles worse at night.,b:Roads are always more slippery at night.,c:Traffic laws are different at night.,d:You cannot see as far ahead at night.
note: Reduced visibility and glare at night limit how far ahead you can see, increasing driving risk.

question: If you plan to turn left at the next corner, to whom must you yield the right-of-way?
options: a:Pedestrians on the sidewalk waiting for a "Walk" signal.,b:Oncoming vehicles also turning left.,c:All approaching vehicles.
note: When making a left turn, you must yield to pedestrians, bicyclists, and vehicles with the right-of-way.

question: To avoid loss of traction on wet roads you should:
options: a:Increase following distance only when visibility is low.,b:Slow down.,c:Make abrupt turns.,d:Apply brakes firmly and abruptly.
note: Reducing speed on wet roads helps prevent hydroplaning and loss of traction; avoid abrupt steering or hard braking.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When traffic is merging into your lane on a freeway, you should:
options: a:Make room for merging vehicles when it is safe to do so.,b:Assert your right-of-way by speeding up.,c:Always maintain your current exact position.,d:Drive onto the shoulder to let them in.
note: When possible and safe, adjust speed or change lanes to allow merging vehicles to enter smoothly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which action should you never do when changing lanes?
options: a:Check your blind spots by looking over your left or right shoulder.,b:Cross the centerline in an intersection.,c:Check for other drivers moving into the same lane.
note: Never attempt to pass or change lanes within an intersection. Always check mirrors and blind spots before changing lanes.

question: When you see a school crossing sign, what should you do?
options: a:Always stop,b:Always sound your horn when you see children.,c:Be alert for children and be prepared to stop.
note: Pentagonal signs mean you are approaching a school zone and/or school crossing. When you see these signs, be alert and prepare to stop.

question: When poor weather or light requires using lights, which should you use?
options: a:Use your high beams.,b:Use your parking lights.,c:Use your low beams.
note: Use low beam headlights in fog, snow, or rain. High beams can reflect back and cause glare in these conditions.

question: A red, octagon-shaped traffic sign always means:
options: a:Stop.,b:Wrong way.,c:Do not enter.,d:Yield.
note: An octagonal sign is always a stop sign; you must come to a complete stop at that sign.

question: When encountering a person crossing with a white cane or guide dog, you should:
options: a:Stop and remain stopped until the person is safely clear of your path.,b:Drive slowly around them.,c:Honk to alert them and then proceed.,d:Yell instructions to help them cross.
note: You must stop and wait until a blind pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog is well clear of your path; always yield to them.

question: Fatigue increases your risk of what?
options: a:Being late for an appointment.,b:Missing an exit.,c:Falling asleep behind the wheel and crashing.
note: Fatigue impairs decision-making and reaction time and can lead to falling asleep while driving, causing serious crashes.

question: You must yield the right-of-way to any pedestrian who is:
options: a:Only in a marked crosswalk.,b:Far from the crosswalk.,c:Standing on the curb.,d:In any crosswalk or intersection.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians who are crossing in marked or unmarked crosswalks and at intersections; always be prepared to yield.

question: Which of the following is the only reliable way to lower your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:Taking a cold shower.,b:Eating high-fat foods.,c:Drinking coffee.,d:Time.
note: Only time allows the body to eliminate alcohol; nothing speeds up the removal of alcohol from the bloodstream.

question: Regulatory traffic signs are typically what color?
options: a:White.,b:Yellow.,c:Green.,d:Blue.
note: Regulatory signs are usually white rectangles or squares with black, red, or green lettering or symbols and indicate laws and rules to obey.
